discovery: Prediction and discovery of flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene (twistronics)

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics: two-dimensional van der Waals materials
motivation: Bistritzer and MacDonald (PNAS 2011) predicted that twisting two graphene sheets to a 'magic angle' near 1.1 degrees collapses the electronic bandwidth into nearly flat bands, where interactions dominate. Jarillo-Herrero and co-workers (Nature 2018) realised this using the tear-and-stack method. They found correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity that could be switched on and off by an electrostatic gate. This work made the twist angle a new control parameter for quantum matter. A single, chemically simple material can now be tuned continuously between insulating, superconducting, magnetic and topological phases. The resulting field of moiré materials has produced orbital ferromagnetism, the quantum anomalous Hall effect and fractional Chern insulators in graphene and transition-metal dichalcogenide moirés. It has changed how condensed-matter physicists design and study strongly correlated electrons. The discovery reveals a controllable physical mechanism and turns stacking geometry into a practical design principle for electronics.
